definitions.explanation: A spouse's parent — either the father-in-law or mother-in-law.
A parent who is not biologically related but has a parental role through remarriage.

examples.japanese: {義理|ぎり}の{親|おや}に{挨拶|あいさつ}した。
{義理|ぎり}の{親|おや}との{関係|かんけい}に{悩|なや}んでいる。
examples.english: I'm struggling with my relationship with my in-laws.

examples.japanese: {正月|しょうがつ}に{義理|ぎり}の{親|おや}の{家|いえ}に{行|い}くのは{緊張|きんちょう}する。
examples.english: Going to my in-laws' house for New Year's makes me nervous.

examples.japanese: {義理|ぎり}の{親|おや}と{仲|なか}がいい。
examples.english: I get along well with my stepparent.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}が{再婚|さいこん}して、{義理|ぎり}の{親|おや}ができた。
examples.english: My mother remarried, and I got a stepparent.

examples.japanese: {義理|ぎり}の{親|おや}を{本当|ほんとう}の{親|おや}のように{慕|した}っている。
examples.english: I look up to my stepparent as if they were my real parent.

notes:
FORMS:
{義理|ぎり} (duty, obligation; in-law) + の (possessive) + {親|おや} (parent)

The {義理|ぎり}の～ pattern is used to form many in-law and step-family terms:
- {義理|ぎり}の{父|ちち}: father-in-law / stepfather
- {義理|ぎり}の{母|はは}: mother-in-law / stepmother
- {義理|ぎり}の{兄弟|きょうだい}: siblings-in-law / stepsiblings
- {義理|ぎり}の{息子|むすこ}: son-in-law
- {義理|ぎり}の{娘|むすめ}: daughter-in-law

FORMAL EQUIVALENTS:
- {義父|ぎふ}: father-in-law (formal)
- {義母|ぎぼ}: mother-in-law (formal)
- {義両親|ぎりょうしん}: parents-in-law (formal)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Relationships with {義理|ぎり}の{親|おや} are a frequent topic in Japanese advice columns and online forums, especially regarding expectations during holidays and family gatherings.
